description:
Goal
Make compiler2 native lowering and codegen consume the settled shared runtime transport model so direct-only callables stay direct across input, call, return, and resume boundaries without allocating or publishing first-class closures.

Problem being fixed
The earlier direct-callable transport bugs from fz-hwn.10, fz-hwn.11, and fz-hwn.12 are fixed. What remains is the same core issue in the last native/codegen seams: downstream code still re-litigates runtime representation decisions that have already been settled upstream.

Verified remaining model holes
1. Native step lowering still forces callable materialization too early.
- In fixtures like `unused_callable_constructor_frontier`, upstream facts already say the callable input is `Omitted`: it is never called, never escapes, and no callable boundary should exist.
- But `src/compiler2/jobs/native.rs` still only distinguishes `DirectOnly` vs materialize-now in `BackendStep::FunctionRef` / `BackendStep::Lambda`.
- That makes native build a first-class callable object even when every downstream layout is omitted, which fails with `native callable materialization ... has no settled callable boundary`.
- Missing state: omitted / never-materialize.

2. Native codegen still lacks an explicit zero-lane delivered shape.
- Upstream/native now permit `return_lane_reprs.len() == 0` when a return is ignored.
- But `src/compiler2/native_codegen/demand.rs` still models delivered shape as only `Value` or `TupleFields`.
- `src/compiler2/native_codegen/terminator.rs` therefore still assumes every non-tuple native return must deliver one value lane, which is false for ignored-return paths like `spawn_then_receive`.
- Missing state: delivered-shape omitted / zero-lane.

3. Some red tests are stale expectation tests, not compiler bugs.
- Example: tests that still require `CallClosure` in native IR even when exact direct-only closures now lower as direct `Call` / `TailCall`.
- These should be updated to assert the settled transport contract rather than the old closure-object path.

Out of scope / separate bug
- The selective-receive artifact panic around original lowered entry ids is a separate artifact seam, not part of this native/codegen transport ticket.

Scope
- Consume settled runtime input, return, resume, capture, and callable-omission layouts in `src/compiler2/jobs/native.rs` end to end.
- Add an explicit zero-lane delivered-shape case in `src/compiler2/native_codegen/*` and thread it through continuation shaping, return emission, and boundary adaptation.
- Keep native local values structural so direct-only callables remain direct until a true first-class boundary demands materialization.
- Keep callable values completely unmaterialized when all downstream layouts are `Omitted`.
- Publish callable boundaries only when native actually materializes a first-class callable object.
- Update stale tests that still assert old closure-object or mandatory delivered-lane behavior.

Code seams
- `src/compiler2/jobs/native.rs`
- `src/compiler2/native_codegen/demand.rs`
- `src/compiler2/native_codegen/terminator.rs`
- `src/compiler2/native_codegen/driver.rs`
- nearby native/codegen tests in `src/compiler2/drive_test.rs`

Removal target
- Delete remaining native helpers that recover callable obligations from lambda/function-ref syntax instead of settled layout/materialization facts.
- Delete codegen assumptions that every native return is either one value lane or tuple-field fast path.
- Delete stale tests that encode the old closure-object path when the settled transport model now proves a direct path.

Checks
- `cargo test --lib compiler2_native_program_`
- `cargo test --lib compiler2_abi_ready_`
- `cargo test --lib compiler2_interp_runs_`
- No native path emits `MakeClosure` / `MakeFnRef` for values whose downstream layouts are all omitted.
- No native/codegen path re-asks whether an ignored return carries a value lane after `return_lane_reprs` has already settled to zero lanes.
- Native JIT/AOT tests pass for spawn/receive, direct lambda call, escaped lambda, opaque callable, enum reducer cases, quicksort, and direct closure-target fixtures.
- Stale expectation tests are rewritten to assert the settled transport contract.

comments.text: Current seam after mirroring demand-shaped local values into native executable inputs and entry captures: native direct-only callable transport still collapses at DeliveredResume because ReturnAbi can only express Value or TupleFields. Repro: compiler2_native_program_jit_runs_enum_reduce_through_compiler2_codegen fails in LowerNativeProgram with 'native call arg 7 for callee 66 expected direct-callable 65 with 0 capture(s), observed Some(Runtime(Var(7)))'. This indicates a direct-only callable returning through a continuation resume boundary and being rebound as a runtime value. Next correct step is to generalize internal return/resume transport from ReturnAbi::{Value,TupleFields} to the same value-layout model used for runtime params/captures, then thread that through artifact planning, backend interpreter DeliveredResume binding, native entry signatures, delivered_args_for_abi, and NativeDemandAbi/codegen delivered-shape handling. Do not restore old closure materialization to satisfy the test.

title: Compiler2 native: lower direct callable demand without first-class closure materialization
